questions.question: The Coromandel plain is located in the _______ direction of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Southern.**__

__
 
• The Coromandel plain is located in the **Southern **direction of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Coromandel Coast** is the southeastern coast region of the Indian subcontinent, bounded by the Utkal Plains to the north, the Bay of Bengal to the east, the Kaveri delta to the south, and the Eastern Ghats to the west.
 
• The Coromandal coast extends over an area of about **22,800** square kilometers.
 
• It may also include the southeastern coast of the island of Sri Lanka.
 
• The coast is generally low and punctuated by the deltas of several large rivers, including the **Kaveri, Palar, Penner, and Krishna **which rise in the highlands of the Western Ghats and flow across the Deccan Plateau to drain into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The alluvial plains created by these rivers are **fertile and favour agriculture**.
 
• The coast is also known for its ports and harbours **Pulicat, Chennai, Sadras, Pondicherry, Karaikal, Cuddalore, Tranquebar, Nagore, and Nagapattinam** which take advantage of their close proximity with regions rich in natural and mineral resources **(like the Chhattisgarh belt and the mines of Golconda and Kolar) and/or good transport infrastructure.**
 
• The Coromandel Coast falls in the **rain shadow of the Western Ghats** and receives a good deal less rainfall during the **summer southwest monsoon**, which contributes heavily to rainfall in the rest of India.
 
• The region averages **800 mm/year,** most of which falls between October and December.
 
• During the winter season, north-east trade winds **prevail over India.**
 
• The Coromandal coast receives winter rainfall because of the **retreating monsoon**
 
• The North-east Monsoon winds pass over the **Bay of Bengal.**
 
• They blow from land to sea and hence, for most parts of the country, it is a** dry season.**
 
• These cause **winter rains** over the plains and **snowfall** in the mountains.
 
• It is because in this region these winds blow from sea to land, thereby carrying moisture along with them.
 
• North-East monsoon is also known as **'October Heat'.**

questions.question: Which of the following statement regarding the Deccan Plateau is correct?

options.text: The Deccan Plateau has almost the same height through its expanse.
The Deccan Plateau is higher on the east and west ends and slopes towards the center.
The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards.
The Deccan Plateau is higher in the east and slopes gently westwards.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Deccan Plateau covers the majority of the southern part of the country.
 
• The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass that lies to the south of the river Narmada.
 
• It is located between three mountain ranges and extends over eight Indian states.
 
• The Plateau covers 422000 sq. km area.
 
• In the south, the plateau is mostly over 1,000 meters above sea level. In the north, it is mostly about 500 m above sea level.
 
• **The Deccan Plateau is higher in the west and slopes gently eastwards.**
 
• One of the distinct features of the Deccan plateau is the black soil area known as Deccan Trap.

 __

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What is the average elevation (in metres) of the Eastern Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**600 - 610**__.

__
 
• The average elevation (in metres) of the Eastern Ghats is 600 - 610 and Western Ghats is from 915 to 1,220 metres .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Eastern Ghats
 
 
• It comprises the discontinuous and low hills that are highly eroded by the rivers such as the Mahanadi, the Godavari, the Krishna, the Cauvery, etc.
 
• Its highest peak is Jindhagada Peak.
 
• Its height is 1690 metres.
 
• Javadi Hills, Palconda range, Nallamala hills, and Mahendragiri hills are some of the important hills of Eastern Ghats.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The East Coastal Plain**

 
 
• This broader coastal plain spreads along the Bay of Bengal from Odisha in the north to Kanyakumari in the south.
 
• Its **northern par**t is known as the **Northern Circars plains** and the** southern part is called Coromandel Coast.**
 
• **Chilka and Pulicat Lakes** are fine examples of lagoons on the east coast.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats**:
 
 
• The Western Ghats are locally known by different names such as ***Sahyadri ***in **Maharashtra**, ***Nilgiri hills*** in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and Annamalai hills,*** Cardamom hills*** in Kerala.
 
• It runs from the south of the valley of river **Tapti to Kanyakumari.**
 
• There are three important passes in the Sahyadris.
 
 
• **Thalghat (between** **Nasik to Mumbai****).**
 
• **Palghat (between Palakkad and Coimbatore).**
 
• **Bhorghat (**between Mumbai and Pune**).**
 
 
 
• The Eastern and the Western Ghats meet each other at the **Nilgiri hills.**

questions.question: Read the given characteristic features of the Indian Desert. Which statement is NOT correct about the Indian Desert?

options.text: It receives 500 mm rainfall per year.
It lies northwest of the Aravalli hills.
It is also known as Marusthali.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It receives 500 mm rainfall per year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Rainfall decreases from the east to the west in Northern India because there is a decrease in the moisture content of the winds.

 
 
• As the moisture-bearing winds of the Bay of Bengal branch of the southwest monsoon move further and further inland, the moisture gradually decreases and results in low rainfall when moving westwards.
 
• Consequently, states like Gujarat and Rajasthan in western India get very little rainfall. 
 
• Rainfall in Rajasthan decreases from South and South-East to North and North-West.
 
 
 
• The Bay of Bengal branch of the Indian monsoon loses its moisture by the time it reaches the north-western part of India where Rajasthan is located.
 
• And the Arabian sea branch of the monsoon flows parallel to the Aravalli Mountains and reaches the northern part of India but does not shed moisture over Rajasthan.
 
• The Rajasthan desert of the Thar Desert in western Rajasthan is the biggest desert in India.
 
 
• The Thar Desert or the Great Indian Desert encompasses about 70% of the total landmass of Rajasthan and hence it is identified as the "Desert State of India".

questions.question: The Himalayas consist of ______ main parallel ranges.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Himalaya is the **youngest fold mountain **range in the world.
 
• The word Himalaya means "**the abode of snow**".
 
• The Himalaya is mostly formed of sedimentary rocks.
 
• The Himalayas consist of **three**__ main parallel ranges, namely:
 
 
• The greater Himalayas.
 
• The lesser Himalayas.
 
• The outer Himalayas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The northernmost range of the Himalaya is known as the **Great Himalayas.**

 
 
• It is also called Himadri.
 
• Himadri is the backbone of the Himalaya.
 
• It is the most continuous range consisting of the loftiest peaks with an average height of 6,000 metres.
 
• It contains all the prominent Himalayan peaks like Mount Everest, Annapoorna, Nandadevi, etc.
 
 
 
• The **Lesser Himalayas **is the mountain range that lies between Himadri and Siwalik.
 
 
• It is also called Himachal.
 
• It is mainly composed of highly compressed and altered rocks.
 
• The altitude varies between 3,700 and 4,500 metres and the average width is 50 Km.
 
• Pir Panjal is the largest range in Himachal.
 
• This region is well known for its hill stations.
 
 
 
• The outermost range of the Himalayas is called the **Shiwalik**(Outer Himalayas.)
 
 
• It extends over a width of 10-50 Km and has an altitude varying between 900 and 1100 metres.
 
• The word Shiwalik literally means "tresses of Shiva".
 
• Shiwalik is parallel to the Ganga plain.
